 Judgment 
KABC070070002017 Presented on : 08-08-2017 Registered on : 08-08-2017 Decided on : 
10-12-2024 Duration : 7 years, 4 months, 2 days IN THE COURT OF THE J U D I C I A L MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS (TRAFFIC COURT - V), BENGALURU Present : VISHWANATH SAVADI B.A., LL.B.,(Hon's) J.M.F.C (TRAFFIC COURT - V) , BENGALURU Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 DATED THIS THE 10 t h DAY OF DECEMBER 2024 Petitioner: Smt.Supriya, W/o.Shantharaju,
Aged about 24 years, Cheeranahalli Village, Kothathi Hobli, Mandya.
(By Sri.R.B.S., Advocate) V/s Respondents: 1. Shantharaju, Aged about 38 years, S/o.Sri.Nataraj.
2. Smt.Leelamma, W/o.Sri.Nataraj.
Both are R/at 4th Main, S.V.G. Nagara, Mudalapalya, Bengaluru.
(By Sri.B.C.R., Advocate) Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed the petition under Section 12 of Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondents for seeking various relief under the Act. 
2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
a. The petitioner submits that her marriage to the first respondent was solemnized on 28-06-2010 at Nudibharathi Samudaya Bhavana, Guthala Road, Mandya. After the marriage, the petitioner stayed with the first respondent for a total of only four months. During this period, she was happy for just one month. Subsequently, the respondents began harassing the petitioner both physically and mentally, primarily in relation to their demand for a dowry of Rs. 5,00,000/-, a car, and a site. 
b. The first respondent (husband) would return late at night, assault the petitioner,
and abuse her with filthy language. He showed no interest in speaking to her and would frequently assault her for trivial reasons. The second Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT respondent (mother-in-law) instigated the first respondent to assault the petitioner and demand additional dowry. She also prevented the petitioner from eating and restricted her ability to communicate freely with her husband. Moreover,
the second respondent interfered in all matters between the petitioner and the first respondent. 
c. On one occasion, at the instigation of the second respondent, the first respondent threw the petitioner out of the matrimonial home on 27-12-2016. The petitioner was forced to seek treatment at Government Hospital, Mandya. Following this, a Supriya vs Shantharaju on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190595043/
1 panchayat was held, and the respondents promised to look after the petitioner better in the future. Despite this, the respondents continued their abusive behavior and assaulted the petitioner once again, driving her out of the house on 09- 02-2017. The petitioner sought medical treatment at K.C. General Hospital and thereafter returned to her parental home. 
d. The petitioner submits that, at the time of marriage, her parents paid Rs. 50,000/-
as dowry, along with gold ornaments, and spent over Rs. 3,00,000/- to perform the Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT marriage as per the respondents' demands. 
However, the first respondent was not satisfied with the dowry and continued to demand an additional Rs. 5,00,000/-, a car, and a site from her parents. 
e. After advice from elders, the first respondent took the petitioner back to his house,
but the respondents continued their cruel treatment. The petitioner was not provided with food, clothing, or other necessities, and was kept isolated in the house. She was also verbally abused, including derogatory comments about her mother. Eventually,
the respondents drove her out of the shared house, leaving her exposed to domestic violence. 
f. The petitioner further alleges that the first respondent invaded her and her parents'
privacy. On one occasion, he approached her parental house and demanded she return with the dowry as per his demands, threatening to kill her if she refused. 
Despite the petitioner and her parents' requests for the first respondent to enter their house and discuss the matter, he refused and assaulted the petitioner. 
Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT g. The petitioner expresses fear that the first respondent may provoke violence against her, especially now that the matter is before the court. As such, she seeks protection orders to prevent further harm. The petitioner is a housewife with no independent income and is entirely dependent on the respondent. The first respondent earns over Rs. 85,000/- per month from his business. Based on these circumstances, the petitioner prays that the petition be allowed. 
3. After receiving notice, the respondents appeared through their counsel and filed their objections to the main petition. 
Respondents' Statement of Objections a. The respondents deny all the allegations made by the petitioner, describing them as false, frivolous, and vexatious. The respondents acknowledge the marriage took place on 28-06-2010 and that they have a five-year-old daughter. They assert that they have always supported the petitioner and have never tortured her physically or mentally. 
Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT The allegations made by the petitioner are completely untrue. 
The respondents maintain that they have always welcomed the petitioner into their home unconditionally. 
Supriya vs Shantharaju on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190595043/
2 b. The petitioner filed a complaint against the respondents in Crime No. 25/2017, which she later withdrew on 01-06-2017, submitting an affidavit to the police stating that they were living happily together after the intervention of elders. This affidavit clearly shows that the petitioner was not suffering from any form of harassment. 
c. Regarding financial matters, the first respondent works as an assistant to his father, who repairs old televisions. His monthly income does not exceed Rs. 10,000. The respondents are responsible for all household expenditures, and there is no surplus income left for them. Therefore, they contend that the petitioner is not entitled to monthly maintenance. 
d. The respondents also state that the petitioner voluntarily left the matrimonial home and is currently residing with her mother. Despite their efforts to reconcile, the petitioner Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT refused to return to the marital home, and therefore, she is not entitled to maintenance. In light of these facts, the respondents pray that the petition be dismissed. 
4. To substantiate her case, the petitioner filed an evidence affidavit in lieu of examination-in-chief and was examined as PW.1. She produced documents marked as Exhibits P.1 to P.6 and subsequently closed her side of the case. Despite granting sufficient time, the respondents did not cross-examined the PW.1. Rejecting the prayer of respondents, the Court issued an order on 14.08.2019 stating that, the cross-examination of PW.1 would be considered as nil and posted the case for respondents side evidence. 
5. The respondents in order to establish their defense, the respondent No.1 was examined as RW.1 and produced documents marked as Ex.R.1 and closing his side of the case. However, the petitioner did not cross- examine RW.1. Noticing the absence of the petitioner, the Court issued an order on 26.09.2024 stating that the cross-examination of RW.1 would Crl. Misc . No.133/2017 JUDGMENT be considered nil and posted the case for arguments. On 22.08.2024 upon the application of petitioner, this Court re- opened the case and permitted the petitioner to cross-examine the RW.1. 
However, again the petitioner did not cross- examined the RW.1. Noticing the absence of the petitioner, the Court issued an order on 03.09.2024 stating that, the cross- examination of RW.1 would be considered as nil and posted the case for petitioner side argument. 
6. I have heard the arguments of respondent side and despite sufficient time, the petitioner has not come forward to address her side arguments. 
7. The points that arise for my consideration are;
1. Whether the petitioner proves that she has been subjected to domestic violence and neglected by the respondents ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for maintenance?
3. What order?

3 Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT 8. The findings of this Court on the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Point No.2 : In the Affirmative in Part.
 Point No.3 : As per final order for the  following : 
 REASONS 9. Point No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, petitioner being legally wedded wife of respondent No.1 has been subjected to cruelty and domestic violence by the respondents. She contended that, her marriage was solemnized on 28-6-2010 at Nudibharathi Samudaya Bhavana,
Guthala Road, Mandya. Out of their wedlock, they have a female child. During the stay of petitioner in the house of respondents, the respondents have given ill-treatment to the petitioner and drove out the petitioner without providing any maintenance. 
10. The petitioner in order to establish her case she herself got examined as PW-1 by filing affidavit evidence in lieu of her examination in chief and in support of her oral evidence she has got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6. Pw.1 deposed about the Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT ill-treatment given by the respondents during her stay in the house of respondents. The petitioner has produced the Ex.P.1 is the Copy of MLC Report issued by K.C.General Hospital, Ex.P.2 is the Discharge Summary dated 28.12.2016, Ex.P.3 is the Certified copy of order sheet in Cr.No.25/2017, Ex.P.4 is the Certified copy of FIR, Ex.P.5 is the Certified copy of the complaint, Ex.P.6 is the certified copy of FIR. Upon perusal of these documents, relationship between the petitioner, her daughter and respondents are not in dispute. 
11. The respondents in order to establish their defense, the respondent No.1 got examined as RW-1 and in support of his oral evidence he has got marked Ex.R.1 is the Certified copy of order sheet,
petition and affidavit in Crl.Misc.No.415/2017.
12. Although the respondents filed detailed objections to the main petition and the first respondent presented evidence in support of their pleadings, they failed to cross-examine the petitioner's witness (PW.1), despite being granted sufficient time to do so. As a result, the petitioner's allegations, as outlined in Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT the petition, are supported by the petitioner's oral testimony, which has remained unchallenged and unrebutted. The respondents did not present any valid reasons to cast doubt on the petitioner's case. In the absence of any effective cross- examination, the petitioner's version of events stands uncontroverted. Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner has successfully established that she has been subjected to domestic violence by the respondents. Additionally, the evidence shows that the respondents have deserted and neglected the petitioner, failing to provide her with the necessary maintenance and support. Given these circumstances, the Court finds no reason to disbelieve the petitioner's case and is inclined to accept the petitioner's version of events as true and credible. With these observations,
this Court answers the point No.1 in the Affirmative.

4 13. Point No.2:- It is important to note that the present petition was filed on 08.08.2017, and during its pendency, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India issued Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT mandatory guidelines in the matter of Rajnesh vs. Neha and others (Criminal Appeal No.
730/2020), dated 04.11.2020. In this landmark judgment, the Hon'ble Supreme Court provided clear and binding guidelines for matrimonial proceedings, specifically concerning claims for monetary relief. The Court ruled that any party seeking monetary relief--whether maintenance,
compensation, or any other financial assistance-- must file an affidavit disclosing their assets and liabilities. This obligation applies not only at the initiation of the proceedings but also during the pendency of the case, ensuring transparency and fairness in the process. Furthermore, the Court emphasized that failure to comply with this mandatory requirement would result in the party being barred from seeking any monetary relief from the other party until such time as the affidavit is filed. 
14. In accordance with these Supreme Court guidelines, this Court issued an order on 17.09.2024,
directing both parties to file their respective affidavits of disclosure of assets and liabilities. 
Recognizing that such compliance might require Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT time, the Court provided both parties with three adjournments, extending the filing deadlines from 17.09.2024 to 22.11.2024. Despite these multiple opportunities, neither party submitted the required affidavits by the specified dates. 
15. On 30.11.2024, after observing the continued non- compliance of both parties in filing the affidavit of disclosure of assets and liabilities, the Court was compelled to pass a further order stating that the petitioner (the wife) would not be entitled to any monetary relief. The Court took this step because the failure to submit the affidavit violated the mandatory guidelines set forth by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, which had made the filing of the affidavit a prerequisite for seeking financial assistance. 
16. Although the petitioner has provided sufficient evidence to substantiate her claim of having been subjected to domestic violence by the respondents, this failure to comply with the Supreme Court's clear guidelines has had significant legal consequences. As a result, despite the petitioner's proof of Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT domestic violence, she has been deemed ineligible to claim any monetary relief, including compensation, maintenance, and rental accommodation, until she fulfills the mandatory disclosure requirement. 
17. However, it is crucial to emphasize that the petitioner's right to seek protection from domestic violence remains unaffected by her failure to file the affidavit. The Court, while disallowing monetary relief, recognizes the seriousness of the petitioner's allegations and her entitlement to legal protection from further harm. Therefore, the petitioner is still entitled to a protection order, as the need for her safety and protection from domestic violence overrides the procedural non- compliance regarding the affidavit. 
18. In conclusion, while the petitioner's non-compliance with the Court's order concerning the affidavit of disclosure has resulted in her ineligibility for any monetary relief, her fundamental right to protection against domestic violence remains intact. The Court has, therefore, allowed the petitioner Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT to receive a protection order, ensuring her safety and Supriya vs Shantharaju on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190595043/
5 well- being. With these observations, this Court answers the point No.2 in Affirmative in Part.
19. Point No.3:- In view of discussion held above, this Court proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 12 of Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act., is partly allowed. 
The respondents are hereby restrained from committing any domestic violence against the petitioner. 
However, the other reliefs prayed for by the petitioner is rejected. 
Office is directed to supply the copy of the order to the petitioner free of cost. 
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, typed by him, corrected by me,
and then pronounced in the Open court on this 10 th day of December 2024)
VISHWANATH SAVADI J U D I C I A L MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS (TRAFFIC COURT - V), BENGALURU.

Ex. P.5 Certified copy of the complaint. Ex. P.6 Certified copy of FIR. 
LIST OF WITNESSES EXAMINED FOR RESPONDENT R.W.1 Shantharaju.

summary.facts:
The petitioner has filed the petition under Section 12 of Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondents for seeking various relief under the Act.
Subsequently, the respondents began harassing the petitioner both physically and mentally, primarily in relation to their demand for a dowry of Rs. 5,00,000/-, a car, and a site.
She also prevented the petitioner from eating and restricted her ability to communicate freely with her husband.
Moreover,
the second respondent interfered in all matters between the petitioner and the first respondent.
The petitioner was forced to seek treatment at Government Hospital, Mandya.
She produced documents marked as Exhibits P.1 to P.6 and subsequently closed her side of the case.
Despite granting sufficient time, the respondents did not cross-examined the PW.1.

summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondents did not present any valid reasons to cast doubt on the petitioner's case.
In the absence of any effective cross- examination, the petitioner's version of events stands uncontroverted.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner has successfully established that she has been subjected to domestic violence by the respondents.
Additionally, the evidence shows that the respondents have deserted and neglected the petitioner, failing to provide her with the necessary maintenance and support.
15. On 30.11.2024, after observing the continued non- compliance of both parties in filing the affidavit of disclosure of assets and liabilities, the Court was compelled to pass a further order stating that the petitioner (the wife) would not be entitled to any monetary relief.
The Court took this step because the failure to submit the affidavit violated the mandatory guidelines set forth by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, which had made the filing of the affidavit a prerequisite for seeking financial assistance.
16. Although the petitioner has provided sufficient evidence to substantiate her claim of having been subjected to domestic violence by the respondents, this failure to comply with the Supreme Court's clear guidelines has had significant legal consequences.
As a result, despite the petitioner's proof of Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT domestic violence, she has been deemed ineligible to claim any monetary relief, including compensation, maintenance, and rental accommodation, until she fulfills the mandatory disclosure requirement.
The Court, while disallowing monetary relief, recognizes the seriousness of the petitioner's allegations and her entitlement to legal protection from further harm.
Therefore, the petitioner is still entitled to a protection order, as the need for her safety and protection from domestic violence overrides the procedural non- compliance regarding the affidavit.
18. In conclusion, while the petitioner's non-compliance with the Court's order concerning the affidavit of disclosure has resulted in her ineligibility for any monetary relief, her fundamental right to protection against domestic violence remains intact.
The Court has, therefore, allowed the petitioner Crl.Misc.No.133/2017 JUDGMENT to receive a protection order, ensuring her safety and Supriya vs Shantharaju on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190595043/
